extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and third-party requesters / patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for citations of prior art and for filing and processing requests for ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents under 37 CFR 1.501/1.510 and related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art citation that is limited to patents or printed publications and includes the requisite citation description qualifies for entry under 37 CFR 1.501(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a citation is filed after the date of an order for reexamination, it may be retained in the Technology Center until the reexamination concludes and will not be considered in that reexamination (but will later be processed for placement in the patent file). See MPEP §2294.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of citation filed by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper prior art citation is filed by the patent owner it should be entered in the file whether filed prior to or after an order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification to the patent owner is necessary when the patent owner files a proper citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑qualifying citation (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation that is not limited to patents or printed publications or that fails to include the requisite citation description does not qualify for entry under 37 CFR 1.501 and should not be entered in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sender (if known) and the patent owner must be notified that the citation is improper and not being entered. Handling of the citation then varies by situation (service on owner, sender identity, duplicate copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling improper third‑party citations — service included
rubrics_metrics.description: If an improper citation by a third party includes an indication of service on the patent owner and the sender is known, return the original citation paper to the third party along with notification of nonentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the identity of the third party sender is not known, discard the original citation papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling improper third‑party citations — service not included, sender known
rubrics_metrics.description: If the improper citation does not indicate service on the patent owner, the sender is known, and a duplicate copy is present, return the original to the sender and send the duplicate to the patent owner with notification of nonentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the duplicate copy required by 37 CFR 1.501(c) is not present, send the original citation papers to the patent owner along with the notification. Send the third party sender a notification that the citation was not entered and that the original citation papers were sent to the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling improper third‑party citations — service not included, sender unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: If the citation does not indicate service, the sender is unknown, and a duplicate copy is or is not present, discard the duplicate (if present) and send the original citation papers to the patent owner with notification of nonentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedures set out in MPEP for handling such cases; unusual problems should be brought to the Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper citation filed by patent owner (pre‑order) and post‑order handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An improper prior art citation filed by the patent owner prior to an order for reexamination should not be entered and should be returned with notification; prior art submission filed by the patent owner after an order should be entered under 37 CFR 1.555 (ex parte) or 37 CFR 1.933 (inter partes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific MPEP flowcharts and bring unusual problems to the Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of court decisions and litigation papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Solicitor’s Office will process notices required by 35 U.S.C. 290 and will accept copies of notices of suits, other proceedings involving the patent, and decisions from litigations for placement in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable items include final court decisions, decisions to vacate or remand, and decisions as to the merits of patent claims. Non‑merit decisions (venue, discovery dates, sanctions) will not be entered and will be expunged. Papers that provide party arguments (e.g., memoranda in support of summary judgment) will not be entered unless they have entry rights in the reexamination proceeding; such material must be submitted via the rule‑provided vehicle. If the volume is excessive, the Office may return/expunge/discard all or part of the submission. Submissions must be bare notice without additional comment or argument; highlighting or underlining goes beyond bare notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of citation on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any submission of a citation of prior art patents or printed publications in a patent file should be served on the patent owner to keep the owner informed of the patent file contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service should be addressed to the correspondence address set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(c). See MPEP §2222 for correspondence address rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination must present a substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must present 'a substantial new question of patentability' under 35 U.S.C. 303(a) for reexamination to be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office determines whether an SNQ is presented; if so, reexamination will be ordered. The request must clearly point out the SNQ and explain how the cited prior art raises it (see MPEP §2216 and §2217). A requester must not argue that the references do not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may, at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent, file a request for ex parte reexamination of any claim based on prior art patents or printed publications (37 CFR 1.510(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Any person' includes corporations and governmental entities. The patent owner may request reexamination but is limited to ex parte consideration of patents/printed publications; other issues (e.g., public use, on‑sale) may require a reissue. The Director may initiate reexamination under 37 CFR 1.520 in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art scope in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art considered in ex parte reexamination is limited to prior art patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other types of prior art (public use, on‑sale) are not proper bases in ex parte reexamination—patent owner should consider reissue for those issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required fee and effect on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must be accompanied by the fee specified in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1). If the request does not include the fee and all required parts, the requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request; failure to comply generally results in no filing date for the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incomplete, the request may be placed in the patent file as a citation (if it complies with §1.501). The filing date is the date when the request satisfies all the requirements of 37 CFR 1.510.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required elements of a request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for ex parte reexamination must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability; (2) identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested with a detailed explanation of pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to each claim; (3) a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon, with English translations of necessary parts of non‑English documents; (4) a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims) in double column format and any disclaimer/certificates; (5) a certification that a copy of the request filed by a non‑owner was served on the patent owner (name/address indicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/57 is encouraged as a transmittal. A requester must list cited prior art in a comprehensive manner (37 CFR 1.98 listing). Copies must be plainly written on only one side of the paper. See MPEP §2214–§2219 for detailed guidance on each element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and application requirement for each SNQ and proposed ground
rubrics_metrics.description: For each identified substantial new question of patentability and each proposed ground of rejection, the request must explain how the cited documents are applied to meet or teach the patent claim limitations to establish the SNQ or proposed ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must apply all of the cited prior art to the claims for which reexamination is requested. The requester may also point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art if appropriate (patent owner may do so).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document copy and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of every cited patent or printed publication and a copy of the entire patent sought to be reexamined must be supplied; non‑English documents must have translations of the necessary parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent copy should reproduce the printed patent (front page, abstract, drawings, specification, claims) in double column format, on only one side of each sheet. Include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service when requester is not the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification must state that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address in §1.33(c), and indicate the name and address of the party served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after reasonable effort, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office with a cover letter explaining the efforts made and why service failed; include clear wording to avoid erroneous duplicate fees (e.g., 'Duplicate Copy... When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible').

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and power of attorney rules for requester
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is filed by an attorney or agent identifying another party on whose behalf the request is filed, the attorney/agent must have a power of attorney from that party or act in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 (and must be a registered patent practitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing will not be delayed for absence of the power of attorney, but proof of authority may be required if questioned. If an attorney files for an entity wishing to remain anonymous, the attorney is the third party requester. All correspondence for a requester other than the patent owner is addressed to the requester's representative unless otherwise specified. A patent owner may not be represented during reexamination by an unregistered person for signing amendments/other papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner requests and proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A request filed by the patent owner may include a proposed amendment in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner includes a proposed amendment, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply; see MPEP §2250.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: No abandonment or withdrawal after complete filing
rubrics_metrics.description: After the request for reexamination, including the full fee, is received in the Office, no abandonment, withdrawal, or striking of the request is possible, regardless of who requests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In limited circumstances (e.g., final court decision where all claims are finally held invalid), a reexamination order may be vacated (see MPEP §2286).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for reexamination requests — period of enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent; the period was set by rule and is determined by adding 6 years to the date on which the patent expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent expiration date considerations include patent term, maintenance fees, disclaimers shortening term, patent term adjustments/extensions under 35 U.S.C. 154, and extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156 for premarket regulatory review. If litigation is instituted within the statute of limitations, requests may be filed after that statute expires as long as the patent remains enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural expectations and limits on litigation tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination statute, regulations, and procedures do not countenance 'litigation tactics' in reexamination proceedings; parties are expected to conduct themselves accordingly and adhere to applicable rules (e.g., 37 CFR 10.18(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not provided for in the reexamination regulations should be filed with an appropriate petition or waiver or not filed. Multiple submissions (e.g., reply and sur‑reply) are not provided for and should be avoided. Examiners should not answer inquiries from third parties about specific proceedings; refer third parties to the TC QAS or CRU SPE. Office employees should not discuss whether particular evidence was considered during a concluded proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public, but the reexamination file is scanned into IFW to provide an electronic copy available via PAIR; any remaining paper files are not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access and copying may be made from the electronic format copy available through PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation on claim enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment in an ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not broaden claim scope; reexamination is focused on re‑evaluating patentability under SNQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and special dispatch requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on the request for reexamination must be made no later than 3 months from its filing. The remainder of proceedings must proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered, a reexamination proceeding will normally be conducted to its conclusion and issuance of a reexamination certificate indicating the status of all claims following reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling voluminous or inappropriate submissions from litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office deems the volume of papers filed from litigations or other proceedings to be too extensive, it may return, expunge, or discard all or part of the submission at its sole discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should limit submissions to what is relevant and provide them without additional comment; resubmit limited material if necessary. Highlighting/underlining goes beyond bare notice and is not permitted.
